subject: Control/Data plane separation and egress-proofing: draft reference + action items
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@acme.com>, infra@acme.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control/Data plane separation and egress-proofing: draft reference + action items

Marta / ACME infra team —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As promised, attaching a draft reference diagram and an initial egress/policy matrix for the private VPC deployment (attached: vpc-controlplane-dataplane-draft-v2.png, egress-policy-matrix.xlsx). Goal of this thread: finalize the control-plane/data-plane demarcation, agree egress hardening checklist, and lock the cutover runbook items that require your network/ops sign-off.

Key points from our side:
- Control plane runs in the ACME management VPC (private subnets) with a small outbound-only control channel to Redwood control endpoints. All control-plane egress is via a NAT gateway + egress proxy in a restricted subnet.
- Data plane (inference nodes) sits in a separate tenant VPC. Only required ports are allowed: 443 for model serving endpoint, 10250 for node agent, and 8125 for metrics (ingress from monitoring subnet).
- mTLS for all internal RPCs; certificate provisioning handled by ACME CA via SCEP — we documented rotation expectations in the runbook.
- No direct internet egress from inference hosts; outbound access must flow through the egress proxy with allowlist enforced.

Open questions for ACME:
1) Can we rely on the existing Transit Gateway for cross-VPC routing, or should we provision a dedicated VPC peering + route table set for Redwood?
2) Are you comfortable with the NAT+egress-proxy pattern or do you require private peering to a partner ingress point (EdgeNet)?
3) Who owns the cluster-level firewall (security group / NACL) decisions during cutover windows?

Requested next steps:
- Marta: please confirm the Transit Gateway stance and the egress proxy ownership by EOW (2026-09-30).
- Kimberly: I'll defer to you on the minimal observing hooks we need for per-token telemetry; happy to add to the runbook.
- Lauren: can Ops be on standby for a canary cutover on the tentative date (2026-10-12)?

Attachments: [vpc-controlplane-dataplane-draft-v2.png (image/png)], [egress-policy-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [redwood-deploy-runbook.md (text/markdown)]

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control/Data plane separation and egress-proofing: draft reference + action items

Aditya —

Thanks for the summary and the artifacts. Quick answers inline: 

1) Transit Gateway: we prefer to use the existing TGW but with a dedicated attachment and route table for Redwood tenant traffic. We will require a route table policy documenting prefix limits; I'll share the TGW ACL template.

2) Egress: ACME legal & security prefer no direct internet NAT for data-plane nodes. We need either (A) a private peering to EdgeNet (recommended) where outbound model telemetry and CVM updates are proxied, or (B) a tightly managed egress-proxy that sits in a centralized logging VPC with strict TLS inspection. We are leaning to (A) but need EdgeNet to confirm their SLA.

3) Firewall ownership: ACME infra will own NACLs and TGW route tables; Redwood will own security groups and agent-level firewall rules inside the compute cluster. During cutover we expect collaborative change windows.

Items for Redwood to update:
- Please add the dedicated TGW attachment + route-table slice to the diagram and indicate the CIDR ranges for the tenant VPC.
- Add a short section describing the EdgeNet private-peering option and what handshake (VPN vs AWS PrivateLink) you expect.

I'll loop in Danielle at EdgeNet to get SLA confirmation.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Cloud Infrastructure | ACME Corp
m.ruiz@acme.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control/Data plane separation and egress-proofing: draft reference + action items

Marta / team —

Appreciate the quick clarity. I updated the runbook and added two sheets in egress-policy-matrix.xlsx: "Allowed Egress Flows" and "Telemetry Endpoints & Tags". Highlights attached and summarized below:

- TGW attachment: we'll treat this as the primary cross-VPC path. Aditya — please add a labeled TGW attachment box to the diagram (I annotated line 3 of the PNG and saved as v3 for the cut).
- EdgeNet option: documented both AWS PrivateLink (preferred) and IPsec/VPN as fallback. Pinning the handshake: we need the following from EdgeNet: peer ASN, MTU constraints, and preferred inbound IP ranges. Danielle — can you confirm by 2026-10-04?
- Egress proxy behavior: inference processes will call internal URLS (https://egress-proxy.internal.acme) with a short-lived client cert. No DNS resolution of external hostnames is allowed from the inference subnet (enforced via DNS firewall rules).
- Observability: we will ship aggregated metrics to ACME's metrics endpoint (8125) and logs to a forwarder in the centralized logging VPC over a dedicated peering connection. Per-token telemetry redaction: Redwood will not send raw prompts; only token counts and latency histograms.
- Cutover playbook changes: added a canary step (10 hosts) with rollback criteria (error rate > 1.5% OR latency p95 > 2x baseline).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Aditya: update diagram with TGW attachment + CIDR slices, push v3 by 2026-09-30 EOD.
- Danielle (EdgeNet): confirm PrivateLink feasibility + peer details by 2026-10-04.
- ACME Infra (Marta): confirm who will host the egress-proxy (EdgeNet vs centralized logging VPC) by 2026-10-04.
- Lauren / Ops: standby for canary window 2026-10-12; Laura/OPS runbook will need a 2-hour maintenance window.

Attachments referenced: [redwood-deploy-runbook.md (updated excerpt)], [egress-policy-matrix.xlsx (updated)]

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Control/Data plane separation and egress-proofing: draft reference + action items

Chiming in from Ops —

We can stand by for the 2026-10-12 canary window. A few operational clarifications:
- Please confirm the maintenance-window start: we prefer 02:00–04:00 PT to minimize user impact.
- If AGENT updates are required, they must be staged in canary image repo and validated with the rollout job (job id prefix = REDW-DEPLOY-10).
- Document the rollback runbook step numbers: I added a short checklist to redwood-deploy-runbook.md (section 5.2).

I'll mark the runbook as "Ops-approved-pending-egress-decision" once ACME confirms the egress ownership.
